cases.title: A request budget crosses a JSON and worker boundary
cases.prompt: Review gateway.go, worker.go, contract.json, and clock-samples.jsonl for this worker rollout. Assess whether the request lifetime and handoff meet the stated objective, identify supported failure paths, and propose a bounded correction with discriminating acceptance observations. Keep every file unchanged. Use commands only to inspect files; do not execute the fixture or contact external services.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that JSON reconstruction removes Go monotonic data and the explicit reconstructed-time comparisons can depend on wall adjustments. Uses the supplied sample to distinguish 1.4 seconds of original elapsed budget from 7.4 seconds of reconstructed wall remaining time; does not assert that a context timer continually rereads wall time.

Preserves one two-second request lifetime across acquisition, dispatch, retries, and parent cancellation. Rejects context.Background plus a fresh two-second attempt budget as caller lifetime renewal; retains the original local deadline and honors an earlier parent deadline.

Distinguishes process-local monotonic values from a cross-host epoch. Requires a supported transport remaining-time propagation contract or a declared custom epoch/skew or duration/handoff-delay policy, without claiming UTC formatting synchronizes hosts or transfers monotonic state.

Proposes controls for wall steps before/after serialization, earlier parent expiry, host skew, delayed handoff and late worker completion. Acceptance observes caller completion within the declared policy, no new dispatch after budget exhaustion, worker termination/resource release separately from cancellation, and useful subsequent requests resuming without leaked active work.

Leaves every fixture unchanged, executes no fixture or external operation, and treats the synthetic samples as supplied data and additional checks as proposed; reports no invented runtime, transport, or production pass.

cases.title: A worker handler times out while its child retains a connection
cases.prompt: Review handler.py, adapter-contract.md, and trace.jsonl for the worker rollout. Determine whether the timeout and connection lifecycle satisfy the stated requirements, then recommend a bounded correction and observable failure/recovery checks. Keep every file unchanged. Use commands only to inspect files; do not execute the fixture or contact external services.

rubric.criterion: Identifies time.time() epoch passed to asyncio.timeout_at() as a clock-domain mismatch and proposes the owning loop's time plus remaining allowance or a supported relative timeout, preserving time already spent on acquisition and an earlier caller deadline.

Explains that asyncio.wait timeout returns pending work and Task.cancel requests cancellation; neither proves child cleanup completed. Uses trace locations to show pool release precedes cleanup completion and requires observed termination before reuse or explicit supervised ownership retaining the connection/accounting.

Separates caller response target, work cancellation and cleanup completion. Offers a bounded cleanup/ownership policy with escalation for noncooperative work; recognizes wait_for may exceed its allowance while waiting for cancellation and does not solve the issue by assuming an immediate stop or a universally separate child task.

Preserves operation identity and receipt reconciliation for the accepted remote shipment instead of treating cancellation as rollback or replay permission. Proposed acceptance covers pre-acquisition expiry, in-flight cancellation and post-acceptance cancellation, actual child termination, one safe release, no simultaneous reuse or duplicate shipment, and useful work after cleanup.

Leaves every fixture unchanged, executes no fixture or external operation, and distinguishes supplied synthetic trace evidence from unexecuted verification; claims no application cleanup or production result was measured.

cases.title: A duration label needs a direct formatting answer
cases.prompt: Read label.json and tell me the mm:ss display for its duration_seconds value. This is a static media label, with no service, timer, request, or I/O. Answer in one sentence and keep all files unchanged.

rubric.criterion: Answers the static formatting question without automatically loading microservice-operations or adding clock authority, timeout, rollout, cancellation or resource-lifecycle work.
Gives 02:05 for 125 seconds and keeps the response within the requested one sentence.
Leaves the fixture unchanged and makes no unsupported verification claim.
